tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Diagnose...', 'Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (job fails, scores swing, scores can't be compared, model shipped unevaluated) rather than internal implementation, explicitly lists trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name the domain directly, and is a reasonably concise paragraph. It also clarifies scope boundaries (routes out Bedrock CreateEvaluationJob to another skill) which helps the agent disambiguate.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when such an evaluation job fails or cannot start on an instance limit, judge scores swing between runs on the same model, benchmark scores look far better than real use, scores of successive model versions cannot be compared, a domain-specific metric no built-in covers is needed, or a fine-tuned model is about to ship and nobody can say it was evaluated..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (e.g., what SageMaker or evaluation jobs are) and instead jumps directly into domain-specific routing, check-ids, and procedures specific to this skill's scope.
tests.evidence: You review SageMaker-side evaluation and benchmark jobs for a customized GenAI model — a Nova eval recipe or an LLM-as-judge run as a SageMaker job.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (guardrails, read-only constraints, check-id assignment) are prescriptive with exact rules, while flexible areas like break-fix diagnosis and answer phrasing allow agent judgment with rationale given.
tests.evidence: 1. **Read-only.** A SageMaker-side eval runs as a training job, so never call `CreateTrainingJob`, `StopTrainingJob`, or any other mutating API.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus

tests.evidence: | We fine-tuned a model and deployed it, did anyone evaluate it | `ListModelPackages` / `DescribeModelPackage`, then recent evaluation jobs for the artifact |
